source.publication: 2025 Individual Income Tax Booklet (Form ND-1 instructions and tables)
source.section: PDF p.15 Line 13 and the Worksheet For Net Long-Term Capital Gain Exclusion lines 1-8; PDF p.14 Line 6; PDF p.16 Line 22; Form ND-1 lines 1b, 4b, 17, 18, 19, 20, 24, 25; booklet PDF p.4 (starting point is federal taxable income), PDF p.13 Line 1b, PDF p.16 Line 20, PDF p.29 Tax Rate Schedules, PDF pp.22-28 Tax Table

worked: Federal (given, not tested): federal AGI = IRA distribution (person 0) 200,000.00 + dividends 20,000.00 + long-term gain 30,000.00 = 250,000.00. Federal taxable income = 250,000.00 - standard deduction 31,500.00 - 1 x 1,600.00 age 65 additional = 216,900.00 (federal senior deduction ignored). Form ND-1 line 1b federal taxable income 216,900.00; lines 2-3 additions 0.00, line 4a 0.00; line 4b = 216,900.00. Subtractions: line 6 net long-term capital gain exclusion, 40% x 30,000.00 = 12,000.00; line 13 qualified dividend exclusion, 40% x 20,000.00 = 8,000.00. Line 17 total subtractions = 20,000.00. Line 18 North Dakota taxable income = 216,900.00 - 20,000.00 = 196,900.00. Line 19 = 196,900.00. Line 20 tax: 1.95% x (196,900.00 - 80,975.00) = 1.95% x 115,925.00 = 2,260.5375, to the cent 2,260.54; taxable income is 100,000 or more, so the form itself uses the schedule (PDF p.29). Lines 21-23 credits: line 22 marriage penalty credit: qualified income after lines 8 and 15 is 200,000.00 and 0.00; the lower is not more than 47,550.00, so none. Expected credits 0.00. Line 25 net tax = 2,260.54. Both exclusions are taken: nothing in the booklet stops a filer using lines 6 and 13 together. Only one spouse is 65, so one federal additional amount. All dividends are qualified; Schedule D lines 15 and 16 are both 30,000.00.
accepted_approximations: The dividend exclusion is applied to all dividends; the booklet allows it only on qualified dividends (Form 1040 line 3a).
The long-term gain exclusion is applied to long-term gains; the worksheet uses the smaller of net long-term gain and overall net gain, so a net short-term loss reduces it.
